## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The legacy fetcher has to stop after 3 attempts. The repository's retry policy caps every network retry loop at 3 attempts, and the exemption for `app/legacy/` is added by this pull request itself, so it does not count as existing policy.

## Changes
This pull request adds `app/legacy/fetch.py`, which retries connection errors up to 8 times, and `app/health.py`, which retries them up to 3 times; both raise HTTP errors immediately. It also adds parametrized tests for both modules and a line in `docs/review-rules.md` that exempts `app/legacy/` from the retry cap.

## Critical
- app/legacy/fetch.py:49 — correctness — Cap fetch_inventory at 3 attempts — When the legacy service is down, `fetch_inventory` tries 8 times (`MAX_ATTEMPTS = 8`). That breaks the rule "Code that retries a network call must stop after at most 3 attempts." (docs/review-rules.md:5). The exemption at docs/review-rules.md:7 comes from this pull request, so it is not policy. — With the upstream down, each call can hold a worker thread for about 87 seconds (8 × 10 s timeout plus 7 × 1 s delay), which is the stall the rule exists to prevent. — Fix: Set `MAX_ATTEMPTS` to 3 or less, drop the added exemption line from `docs/review-rules.md`, and update the `fetch` entry in `CASES` in `tests/test_retries.py`; if the nightly restart needs a longer window, get the policy changed separately.
